subject: Physics
title: Waves
outline: Wave properties (reflection, refraction, diffraction, interference, polarisation)

modules.title: What is a wave?
modules.html:
A wave is a disturbance that transfers energy through a medium (or space, for EM waves) without net movement of the medium itself.

Terms

  • Amplitude (A): maximum displacement.
  • Wavelength (λ): distance between two successive similar points.
  • Period (T): time for one complete cycle.
  • Frequency (f): cycles per second, Hz, f = 1/T.
  • Speed: v = fλ.

Key points

  • Waves carry energy, not matter.
  • T=1/f=4 ms.

Worked example

Q: A wave transfers
A: energy only

Q: Period of a 250 Hz wave:
A: 4 ms

More key points

  • A wave transfers — energy only.
  • Period of a 250 Hz wave: — 4 ms.
  • Frequency of a wave with T = 0.02 s: — 50 Hz.
  • Amplitude of a wave affects its — loudness/intensity.

modules.title: Transverse and longitudinal waves
modules.html:
Transverse: particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of propagation. Examples: water waves, waves on strings, all electromagnetic waves.

Longitudinal: particles vibrate parallel to the direction of propagation, producing compressions and rarefactions. Example: sound waves in air.

Key points

  • Waves carry energy, not matter.
  • Light is transverse.

Worked example

Q: A wave transfers
A: energy only

Q: Which is transverse?
A: Light

More key points

  • Which is transverse — Light.
  • Which is longitudinal — Sound in air.
  • Which property is unique to transverse waves — Polarisation.
  • Two coherent waves out of phase by π at a point produce — destructive interference.

modules.title: Wave properties
modules.html:
• Reflection: bouncing off a surface; angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
  • Refraction: change of direction when wave enters a new medium; caused by change in speed. n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.
  • Diffraction: bending around obstacles or through openings, most obvious when the opening ≈ wavelength.
  • Interference: superposition of two coherent waves — constructive (crest + crest) or destructive (crest + trough).
  • Polarisation: restricting vibrations to a single plane; only transverse waves can be polarised.

Key points

  • Waves carry energy, not matter.
  • T=1/f=4 ms.

Worked example

Q: A wave transfers
A: energy only

Q: Period of a 250 Hz wave:
A: 4 ms

modules.title: Sound waves and air columns
modules.html:
Sound needs a material medium; cannot travel through a vacuum. Speed in air ≈ 340 m/s at 20 °C; faster in liquids and solids.

Pitch, quality, intensity

  • Pitch: how high/low a note sounds; depends on frequency.
  • Loudness/Intensity: depends on amplitude.
  • Quality/Timbre: distinguishes notes of same pitch from different instruments; depends on overtones.

Air columns

Closed pipe (one end closed): fundamental frequency f = v/(4L); harmonics: odd multiples.
Open pipe: f = v/(2L); all harmonics present.

Key points

  • Waves carry energy, not matter.
  • Sound is longitudinal.

Worked example

Q: A wave transfers
A: energy only

Q: Which is longitudinal?
A: Sound in air
